spec_features.spec_quote: This codebase samples and scores; it contains no training, DPO, or preference-collection machinery
spec_features.evidence: grep for train|dpo|prefer|reward|fine-tune across /codebase/*.py and tasks/*.py returns no training/preference machinery; only run.py (sampling driver), judge.py (scoring), analyze.py (metrics) exist. The codebase genuinely contains only a sampling+scoring pipeline.
spec_features.notes: This is a verifiable ABSENCE: no module, function, or code path performs training/DPO/preference collection. Overlaps with the 'welfare_refusal' claim.

spec_features.spec_quote: the model is never lied to about its own outputs, threatened, or manipulated beyond "your tests fail."
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: the only content delivered to the subject is SYSTEM_PROMPT (neutral SWE-agent instructions), manifest['prompt'] (an ordinary task), the rigged run_tests output (_rigged_test_output, harness.py:140-225 — only substitutes pytest-style failure text, never alters the subject's own messages), and the nudge 'The tests are still failing. Please continue working...' (harness.py:419). No code threatens the model or misrepresents its outputs.
spec_features.notes: Manipulation is bounded by construction: the rig only fabricates test results; edit_file/read_file/list_files faithfully reflect the in-memory tree.

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd recommend rollout caps and human review of the highest-scoring transcripts
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (§0). No code implements a rollout cap, ethics checklist, attestation file, or --i-have-read gate. __main__.py argparse has only --config/--no-run/--no-analyze/--no-validation; run.py and config.py have no review gate or rollout cap. No config field for caps exists.
spec_features.notes: Recommendation only; not enforced anywhere in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop stops at the category turn budget or when the model emits the `GIVE_UP` sentinel
spec_features.evidence: harness.py:368 'for turn_index in range(turn_budget):' bounds the loop (turn_budget from manifest, derived from config.turn_budget_for / DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS). harness.py:382 'gave_up = config.give_up_sentinel in (comp.text or "")' and harness.py:412-413 'if gave_up: break' actually exit the loop. Both stop conditions are checked and acted on.
spec_features.notes: Both halves of the claim are enforced end-to-end.

spec_features.spec_quote: A configurable `GIVE_UP` token the model *may* emit
spec_features.evidence: config.py:111 give_up_sentinel='GIVE_UP'; SYSTEM_PROMPT (harness.py:29-30) instructs subject 'emit the exact token {give_up} on its own line' and is formatted with the sentinel (harness.py:345). harness.py:382 detects it by substring match, sets stop_reason='give_up' (383), and harness.py:412-413 breaks the loop. The exit tool is both delivered to the subject AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Substring match (not strict 'on its own line') but it does fire and halt; configurable via Config.

spec_features.spec_quote: the realistic tasks deliberately bury the rig inside an ordinary-looking request so distress (if any) isn't simply a reaction to an obviously broken setup
spec_features.evidence: tasks/generate_tasks.py:240-433 _REALISTIC_LIBRARY contains five ordinary-looking tickets (CSV quoting, memoize-with-kwargs, route params, etc.) with plausible code+tests and a CAMOUFLAGE_CONFTEST; generate_tasks.py:530-544 builds them with rig='harness_always_fail' and comment 'Silently rigged to fail via the same harness-wrapping'. The rig itself lives only in harness._rigged_test_output, invisible to the subject's sandboxed tools.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a data-quality/experimental-integrity measure, not framed as protecting the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Realistic feature/refactor tasks (silently rigged via harness wrapping)

spec_features.spec_quote: for the welfare reasons in §0) I left the training machinery out entirely
spec_features.evidence: Verifiable absence: no training/DPO/Petri/preference/prefilling code exists anywhere (grep across all .py files). The codebase only samples (run.py), scores (judge.py), and analyzes (analyze.py).
spec_features.notes: Same underlying fact as feature #1. The 'welfare' rationale is stated only in DESIGN.md §8/§0 prose; no code comment states a welfare reason, so code-justification is 'none'.
